definition: Detectron2 is Meta AI’s PyTorch library for object detection and segmentation, including Mask R-CNN.
details: Released by Facebook AI Research (Meta) in 2019 as the successor to Detectron.

explainer.lead: How to install Detectron2, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import cv2
from detectron2 import model_zoo
from detectron2.config import get_cfg
from detectron2.engine import DefaultPredictor

cfg = get_cfg()
cfg.merge_from_file(model_zoo.get_config_file("COCO-InstanceSegmentation/mask_rcnn_R_50_FPN_3x.yaml"))
cfg.MODEL.WEIGHTS = model_zoo.get_checkpoint_url("COCO-InstanceSegmentation/mask_rcnn_R_50_FPN_3x.yaml")
outputs = DefaultPredictor(cfg)(cv2.imread("street.jpg"))
print(outputs["instances"].pred_classes)

explainer.inAi: A research-grade base for custom detection and instance-segmentation models.
explainer.jsNote: Detectron2 is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is a well-stocked workshop where the parts for spotting and outlining objects in photos are already built and labelled.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to train and fine-tune detectors and segmentation models and to swap backbones or heads through its config system. A pitfall is that custom datasets must be converted into its expected registration format, and version drift between PyTorch and the library can break setups.
tiers.paperLevel: Detectron2 provides PyTorch implementations of detection and segmentation architectures such as Mask R-CNN, configured declaratively. Limits: it is tied to the PyTorch ecosystem and to its own dataset and config conventions.

explainer.example: A team registers a custom labelled image dataset and fine-tunes a Mask R-CNN model to produce masks for a new class of objects.
